title: Three representative directions
reading: The slide lays out three representative directions in computer vision, organized around the relationship between an image/video and a 3D/4D scene: recognition, reconstruction, and generation. A figure credited to Torralba, Isola, and Freeman illustrates the mapping between a scene and its projection surface. A note adds that language can enter at the middle of any of these stages.

visuals.description: Diagram contrasting image/video with 3D/4D scene, with a projection surface between them, annotated with three numbered arrows/paths: 1 Recognition, 2 Reconstruction, 3 Generation. Credited to Torralba, Isola, and Freeman, Foundations of Computer Vision.
visuals.assertion: Recognition, reconstruction, and generation are three directions of mapping between images/videos and 3D/4D scenes via a projection surface.

concepts.name: Recognition
concepts.why_it_matters: One of the three core directions: inferring semantic content from images.

concepts.name: Generation
concepts.why_it_matters: Synthesizing images/videos from scenes or other inputs.

concepts.name: Projection surface
concepts.why_it_matters: The imaging plane linking 3D scenes to 2D observations.

concepts.name: Role of language
concepts.why_it_matters: Language can be injected at intermediate stages of any of the three directions.

verbatim_spans: Language can play in the middle of any stages!
